subject: On-prem egress peering, warm-pool provisioning, and GPU-rightsizing for Velox
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@velox.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sizing ask: on-prem GPU pool + egress peering requirements

Hi Aditya —

We dug into forecasted Q4 traffic and need a concrete plan for the on-prem private deployment you're proposing. High level:
- Sustained inference: 2.5M tokens/day (roughly 30 requests/sec avg, 95th pct spikes to ~220 req/sec).
- Typical tail latency target: P95 < 120 ms token (application-level P95 generation time < 400ms).
- Burst windows: 5–10 minute spikes up to 1,200 concurrent request contexts (many are short seqs ~64 tokens).
- Egress limits: our colo has a single 10 Gbps egress pipe today; pref to keep peak egress under 8 Gbps.
- Preferred peering: direct cross-connect or VPC peering; we need BGP failover if direct link flaps.

Attached is our demand profile (velox-demand-profile.csv). Can you provide:
1) Sizing recommendation (GPU pod count, slab allocation, warm-pool sizing) to meet P95 targets with 20% safety margin.
2) Network plan: peering options, NAT/egress design, expected egress at 95th/99th percentile.
3) Operational items: warmup checklist, cache/kv warm strategies, expected quantization trade-offs.

CCing our infra ops group (velox-ops) on timeline. We are aiming to have a mutual action plan by EoW.

Thanks,
Nina
Nina Patel
Head of Infrastructure, Velox AI
[attachment: velox-demand-profile.csv (csv)]

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sizing ask: on-prem GPU pool + egress peering requirements

Aditya / Markus — first-pass sizing and network notes below (high level). I tested calculations against Velox profile in the CSV; details in attached sizing-matrix.csv.

Summary recommendations:
- Service profile: optimize for short-context inference (avg seq 64 tokens). Use medium-A100 equivalent nodes with 80 GB per node for MXNet/TF runtime; recommend 8 pods per slab (pod = 1 GPU).
- Baseline capacity: 12 slabs (96 GPUs) for sustained QPS to hit avg 30 rps with concurrent warm pools to accommodate normal spikes up to 220 rps.
- Burst headroom: keep a warm-pool of 6 slabs (48 GPUs) in standby for 5–10 minute spikes; admission control to shed non-critical low-score requests at >500 concurrent contexts.
- Safety margin: 20% across compute and network, so operational target = 115 GPUs reserved (round up to next procurement unit).

Network / egress:
- Estimated egress at 95p: ~4.6 Gbps (token serialization + embeddings), 99p could touch ~7.1 Gbps during bursts; safe cap under 8 Gbps but advise direct cross-connect to avoid extra egress hops.
- BGP failover: prefer primary cross-connect + VPC peering fallback over public internet; configure route-preference with shorter local-pref on fallback. Implement BFD for sub-100ms fail detection.
- NAT sizing: edge NAT cluster sized for ~1.5x concurrent contexts (recommend 2 x NAT boxes for HA), connection tracking tuned for short-lived connections.

Operational items:
- Warm-pool strategy: keep KV-cache pre-warmed for top 20 prompt prefixes (per Velox sample), background cache warming after deploys. Warm-pool prefetch window 3–5 minutes.
- Quantization: 4-bit q8_0 gives ~1.6x throughput but increases variance in tail latencies; use for non-critical routes, keep fp16 for critical P95 workloads.

Attachments: sizing-matrix.csv (detailed calc), egress-topology-diagram.png (proposed cross-connect + fallback).

If this looks reasonable I'll draft a mutual action plan and cost estimate.

— Lauren
Lauren Bishop
Product Manager, Redwood Dedicated
[attachments: sizing-matrix.csv, egress-topology-diagram.png]

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>, lauren_bishop@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 10 Aug 2026 10:35:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sizing ask: on-prem GPU pool + egress peering requirements

Quick tech notes / caveats to Lauren's draft:
- Warm-pool churn: 48 GPUs warm standing will increase memory fragmentation over time if we keep varying model sizes. Recommend strict model pinning for warm-pool or use fast container reuse (instance reuse) to avoid OOM churn.
- Cold-start cost: measured warmup times for large context models ~2.2s (+/- 0.4s) per container on our infra; that implies admission control thresholds need to consider token amortization for short bursts.
- Quantization trade: 4-bit improves throughput but increases worst-case decode iterations for some instruction sequences — I suggest A/B test on a slice of traffic first.
- Network: carrier-level cross-connect will reduce jitter; ensure flow-labeling and QCI mapping at colo if they support it. Also, ensure sFlow telemetry is forwarded to Redwood Console for per-route latency breakouts.

Proposed action: schedule a 30-min technical sync with Velox ops to walk the topology and validate the 8 Gbps constraint and maintenance windows.

Attaching a quick ops checklist.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Infrastructure Lead, Redwood Inference
[attachment: warmup-ops-checklist.md]

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@velox.ai>, velox-ops@velox.ai
Cc: lauren_bishop@redwood.ai, markus_klein@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 10 Aug 2026 13:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Proposed plan & next steps — Velox on-prem GPU pool sizing

Hi Nina — thanks for the profile. Based on our review (summary below) we propose the following initial commitment and runbook to meet your latency & burst requirements. Full calculations attached in the mutual action plan.

Proposed commitment (initial):
- Procurement/Reserve: 128 GPUs (16 slabs of 8 GPUs) installed in your colo. Operational reserve = 115 GPUs (compute headroom + 20% safety).
- Warm-pool: maintain 48 GPUs in standby for 5–10 minute bursts (auto-spin-up policy to scale to full reserve within 90s).
- Admission control & SLAs: soft-shed starting at 500 concurrent contexts; hard admission at 1,200. Application P95 committed < 400ms for reserved capacity.

Network & egress: 
- Primary: 10 Gbps direct cross-connect. Reserve: VPC peering over redundant links with route preference (BGP + BFD). Expected 99p egress during bursts ~7 Gbps; staying under 8 Gbps.
- NAT/Edge: 2 NAT nodes in active-passive, connection tracking tuned for short connections, sFlow to Redwood Console for per-route telemetry.

Operational checklist:
- Warm-pool pre-warm top 20 prompt prefixes post-deploy.
- Quantization testing plan: start with fp16 on critical routes; roll q4_0 on non-critical routes after A/B validation.
- Telemetry: enable token-level tracing for first 48 hours of ramp.

Next steps:
1) Confirm maintenance window options (Mon–Thu nights preferred).
2) Technical sync (30 min) with Velox ops to validate cross-connect and IP addressing (suggest Wed 11 Aug, 11:00 PT).
3) Sign mutual-action-plan and SOW.

I've attached the mutual-action-plan.pdf and the drive link with the detailed sizing sheet. If that timeline works, I'll schedule the sync and loop in procurement.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Enterprise Solutions, Redwood Inference
